reEstimate: Planned 1–3 active days after root cause; root cause and fix in one session.

rootCause.summary: Every glyph cluster is drawn by slicing the line's single raster (one fillText of the whole shaped run) at the cluster's rounded advance boundaries (drawCluster). A glyph whose ink overhangs its advance (Source Serif's v and i serifs at tracking −35) is split: the overhang belongs to the neighbour's slice. While all clusters share one pose the slices tile the raster exactly, so static text is correct. As soon as neighbours have different poses (per-glyph entrance offsets or opacity, the hold's tracking animator, roll transitions), the overhang moves and fades with the neighbour: a detached fragment beside it and a seam in the glyph it was cut from. This matches the plan's candidate (overhang clipping when per-glyph slices change position).
rootCause.evidence: Oracle test on main 0af3a405 (tests/browser/composition-glyph-seams.ts, lossless PNG renders, 'v' + 'e' in the T1 style): with the 'e' transparent, 188 px of the 'v' are missing; with the 'e' dropped 300 px or spread 40 px, 376 px differ (the 188 missing plus the same 188 px travelling with the 'e'). Pairs 'li' 70 px, 'iv' 164 px, 'Ol' 0 px. A zero-offset animator renders pixel-identically to the static draw. The proof's t1-entrance-serif-fragment.jpg shows the travelling piece of the 'v' serif left of the rising 'e'.

fix.summary: drawRaster finds lines whose clusters are not all drawn with one pose (position, transform, opacity, blur, stroke, fill, font axes, mask). On those lines, each run of neighbouring clusters that share a pose (a glyph under per-glyph motion, a word under word motion) is drawn from its own raster: the segment's text shaped and painted as one run at its layout position, shifted by an integer so subpixel phases and the unscaled draw are kept. The segment raster holds only its own glyphs' ink, overhangs included. Lines with one shared pose keep the line raster's slices, so settled text is unchanged.
details: Segment rasters are made on first use while drawing, cached per segment (first:last) on the line raster or its font-axis variant, and released with it. They are painted locally rather than through the shared preparation pixel source, which only admits requests during preparation, and retained so a frame's scratch memory does not reclaim them.
Their tints and outlines are local caches on the segment raster, as the existing colour cache does when shared capacity is exceeded.
A first version isolated each cluster separately; it was replaced before commit because a ligature inside a word moving as one would have been drawn unligated (see rejectedExperiments).

rejectedExperiments.experiment: Isolate every cluster separately (a raster per glyph).
rejectedExperiments.reason: Removed the seams, but a ligature inside a word moving as one unit would be drawn as separate glyphs while the word moves and as a ligature once settled. Replaced by same-pose segments, which keep shaping inside the unit.

rejectedExperiments.experiment: Segment rasters through the shared preparation pixel source (CanvasPixelSource), like line rasters.
rejectedExperiments.reason: The composition export's source cache admits new requests only inside the preparation retry loop; a request made while drawing throws a pending source ('Unexpected failure' on P1 export). Isolated rasters are painted locally instead.

rejectedExperiments.experiment: Local segment canvases without retaining them.
rejectedExperiments.reason: The managed render memory reclaims canvases allocated during a frame's scratch phase; the cached canvas was zero-sized on a later frame (P1 export: drawImage of a canvas with width or height 0). Retained like local tints.

rejectedExperiments.experiment: Even/odd phase rasters (two extra full-line rasters).
rejectedExperiments.reason: Not built: an overhang can reach past a narrow neighbour (i, l) into the next cluster of the same phase, so it does not isolate glyphs in general.

limitations: Segment rasters are not counted in the 128-megapixel preparation budget; each covers its glyphs plus padding and is made only for lines with distinct poses. Since review fix 1 they are bounded per raster to the most recently used max(32, 2 × clusters).

A ligature whose components have different poses is cut at the layout advance (review fix 3): its pieces move with their own glyphs, as one glyph cannot take two poses. This keeps its settled shape instead of reshaping it as separate letters.
Every animated frame with distinct per-glyph poses changes pixels (the intended fix); the renderer version bump versions it.

findings.finding: Isolated segment cache grew without bound (keyed first:last, kept until disposal; a stagger adds a wider settled-prefix segment each time it grows, arbitrary motion up to N(N+1)/2).
findings.fix: Most-recently-used bound per raster, max(32, 2 × clusters), via cachedRecent (packages/renderer-core/src/recent-cache.ts, unit-tested). Evicted segments release canvas, outlines and local tints through releaseTextRaster, now shared with disposal. No pixel change.
findings.commit: fix(typography): bound the isolated-segment cache (ET5b review 1)

findings.finding: A segment whose clusters have different span colours but one animated fill was tinted only if the first cluster's span colour differed from the fill.
findings.fix: drawSegment draws as painted only when every drawn cluster's span colour is the fill. Reachable only on source-colour rasters (composition layers with rasterize: source-colors); colour-coverage rasters were unaffected. Oracle case 'tinted': 7,776 px off on the previous code, 0 after.
findings.commit: fix(typography): tint a mixed-colour segment as a whole (ET5b review 2)

findings.finding: Segments are shaped alone, so a ligature or contextual form across a pose boundary was drawn as separate glyphs while poses differed and snapped back on settle.
findings.fix: joinsNext measures once per boundary whether shaping joins a cluster to the next (pair shaped together vs each alone, at layout positions; kerning does not count). Clusters joined across a pose boundary draw as advance-cut slices of one joined-unit raster with their own poses. Oracle case 'joined' (fi with only the i displaced; reassembly equals the static ligature): 1,656 px off on the previous code, 0 after. CE0 typography/glyph-performance re-recorded: its 'office' ffi ligature keeps its settled form in frames 0-59 (62-167 px per sampled frame). ET0 --check unchanged.
findings.commit: fix(typography): keep joined glyphs whole across pose boundaries (ET5b review 3)
